findings.why_it_matters: The heading levels invert the clause hierarchy. 16.2.1.2 is a fourth-level clause but is emitted at h2 - shallower than its own parent 16.2.1, which is at h3, and shallower than its sibling 16.2.1.1, which is at h4. Likewise 16.2.2 (third level) is at h2 while its peer 16.2.1 is at h3, and 16.2.2.1 / 16.2.2.2 (fourth level) sit at h3 while their peer 16.2.1.1 sits at h4. Any tool that builds an outline, a table of contents, or a section-anchored citation index from the markdown headings will place 16.2.1.2 and 16.2.2 as top-level peers of the '## Page NNN' furniture rather than inside clause 16.2, so a spec-citation lookup walking the heading tree can fail to resolve 16.2.1.2 and 16.2.2.x.
